findings.failure_path: Two parallel skill loads with no callID (A then B) are queued for the same session and tool. If B's tool.execute.after arrives first, skill-name matching discards A's queued entry and deletes its pendingSkills key. A's after then takes the wrong entry or falls back to 'unknown-call', so a real skill load goes unrecorded and a later Task dispatch is wrongly blocked.
findings.smallest_fix: When the name matches, remove only the matched entry with queue.splice(idx,1); leave the earlier entries queued and their pendingSkills intact, and rely on the 64-entry cap and session cleanup to bound orphans.

findings.failure_path: The E2E row reports 'GitHub Actions 8/8 polled after branch push' as passing, and plan.md marks AC-4 verified, but no CI result is recorded and section 7 shows review still pending, so the composite action's behavior on real runners is claimed without evidence.
findings.smallest_fix: Mark the CI row and AC-4 as pending until a run URL or ID and its result for this candidate are recorded.

concern_results.conclusion: AC-1..AC-7 surfaces are present in the diff. Stamp cache, R0 hint, parallel repo-gates, composite action, tsconfig, callID FIFO, pack-suite move and raw docstring match the stated intent. One edge-case pairing issue is listed under failure_paths.

The cache directory must be a non-symlink, owned by the current user and exactly 0700, and stamps are written atomically. Failed or skipped self-tests never write a stamp. The ripgrep SHA-256 is checked again after a cache hit, before install. The R0 hint never runs anything under ~. No unsafe write path found.

Rollback when tool.execute.before throws, the 64-entry caps and per-session cleanup are present. Problem: dequeueSyntheticCall's skill-name matching discards older queued entries, so when parallel skill loads with no callID complete out of order, the earlier calls lose their pending state.

The cache suite, R0 hint assertion, -W error check, package.json metadata test and callID pairing/rollback/cap tests would each fail against the risky behavior. No test covers out-of-order parallel skill loads with no callID.

Scope stays within B2-1..B2-4. The composite action now sets up Python 3.12 in regression-fast and regression-heavy, where those jobs previously used the runner's system Python; this is acceptable. Output tokens are preserved.
The change can land as one PR and be reverted with git revert. Cache bypass flags exist. The pack-suite rename and the test:pack script change ship in the same change.
The alias_audit_unavailable message gives a usable fix hint. Parallel suites run under the repo_gates label. The CI install step reports version and digest mismatches.

Contract docs (root AGENTS.md, packages/opencode-plugin/AGENTS.md, skill scripts AGENTS.md) are updated to match the new commands. No change loosens a contract. Evidence of an independent review is still pending (section 7), but it is declared as pending.
